import Mathlib

/-!
# Entropy-Complexity Bridge: From Compression to Information Bounds

This file establishes formal bridges between algorithmic compression/complexity
and entropy-like information bounds on finite types. The central theme is:

> **Compression controls entropy-like support complexity.**
> If a finite family of objects can be injectively encoded into a bounded
> code space, then the family's cardinality (and hence its log-cardinality,
> a uniform entropy surrogate) is bounded by the code space size.

## Main Results

### Finite cardinality bounds from injective encodings
- `card_le_of_injective_to_fin`: Injective map to `Fin N` bounds cardinality by `N`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code`: Injective map to `Fin (2^k)` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode`: Injective map to `Fin k → Bool` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound`: Range of a map to `Fin (2^k)` has size ≤ `2^k`.

### Entropy bounds
- `EntropyBound`: Predicate `Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k`, the finite uniform entropy inequality.
- `entropyBound_of_injective_code`: Injective code implies entropy bound.
- `uniform_entropy_le_code_length`: Log-cardinality bounded by code length.

### Support monotonicity (data processing)
- `support_entropy_monotone_under_map`: `|range f| ≤ |α|`.
- `card_range_le_card_codomain`: `|range f| ≤ |β|`.
- `support_entropy_comp_monotone`: `|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|` — deterministic data processing.

### Cross-domain bridge
- `complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound`: Connects compressor bounds
  to finite cardinality control.

## Mathematical Significance

These theorems form the combinatorial skeleton of the source coding principle
and create a formal route from Kolmogorov-style complexity bounds to
entropy/information inequalities. The composition monotonicity theorem
`support_entropy_comp_monotone` is a combinatorial shadow of the
**data processing inequality**: deterministic post-processing cannot
increase the number of distinguishable outputs.
-/

open Set Function Finset Fintype

/-! ## Section 1: Core Finite Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- An injective map from a finite type to `Fin N` implies the source has
at most `N` elements. This is the fundamental counting principle underlying
all compression-to-entropy arguments. -/
theorem card_le_of_injective_to_fin
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {N : ℕ}
    (f : α → Fin N) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ N := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin N) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = N := Fintype.card_fin N

/-- An injective encoding into `Fin (2^k)` bounds source cardinality by `2^k`.
This is the exponential form of the entropy bound: if objects can be
described by `k`-bit codes, there are at most `2^k` of them. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k :=
  card_le_of_injective_to_fin enc henc

/-- The cardinality of the function space `Fin k → Bool` is exactly `2^k`.
This witnesses bitstrings of length `k` as a code space of size `2^k`. -/
theorem fintype_card_fun_bool (k : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) = 2^k := by
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]

/-- An injective encoding into explicit bitstrings `Fin k → Bool` bounds
cardinality by `2^k`. This is the most concrete form: each element gets
a unique `k`-bit string, so there can be at most `2^k` elements. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (f : α → (Fin k → Bool)) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = 2^k := fintype_card_fun_bool k

/-- The range of any map into `Fin (2^k)` has at most `2^k` elements.
This does not require injectivity — it bounds the number of distinguishable
outputs of any encoding scheme. -/
theorem card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound
    {n k : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin (2^k)) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^k)) := Fintype.card_subtype_le _
    _ = 2^k := Fintype.card_fin _

/-! ## Section 2: Entropy Bound Predicate and Logarithmic Form -/

/-- `EntropyBound α k` asserts that the uniform entropy of the finite type `α`
is at most `k` bits: equivalently, `|α| ≤ 2^k`. This is the finite
combinatorial skeleton of the source coding bound `H(X) ≤ k` for a
uniform source over `α` encoded with `k`-bit codewords. -/
def EntropyBound (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k

/-- An injective encoding into `k`-bit codes implies the entropy bound.
This is the formal finite-uniform entropy inequality: if every element
of `α` receives a unique `k`-bit code, then `H(α) ≤ k`. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    EntropyBound α k :=
  card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc

/-
Logarithmic form of the entropy bound: if `α` injects into `Fin (2^k)`,
then `log₂ |α| ≤ k`. Uses `Nat.log` which is the floor of the logarithm.
-/
theorem uniform_entropy_le_code_length
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k := by
  -- We have card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code which gives Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k.
  -- Taking the base-2 logarithm is monotonic, so log₂ |α| ≤ log₂ 2^k = k.
  have hcard : Fintype.card α ≤ 2 ^ k := by
    apply card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc
  exact (Nat.log_mono_right hcard).trans (Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2) k).le

/-- For any injective encoding `α → Fin (2^k)`, the
log-cardinality of `α` is bounded by `k`. -/
theorem log_card_range_le_of_embedding_into_bitstrings
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k :=
  uniform_entropy_le_code_length enc henc

/-! ## Section 3: Support Monotonicity — Data Processing -/

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as its domain.
This is a combinatorial form of the principle that deterministic
processing cannot create new distinguishable outputs. -/
theorem support_entropy_monotone_under_map
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card α :=
  Fintype.card_range_le f

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as the codomain.
This is the trivial but useful fact that range ⊆ codomain implies
the cardinality inequality. -/
theorem card_range_le_card_codomain
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card β :=
  Fintype.card_subtype_le _

/-
**Combinatorial Data Processing Inequality.**
Composition cannot increase the number of distinguishable outputs:
`|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|`. This is the finite combinatorial
shadow of the data processing inequality `H(g(X)) ≤ H(X)` for
deterministic channels.
-/
theorem support_entropy_comp_monotone
    {α β γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range (g ∘ f)) ≤ Fintype.card (Set.range f) := by
  -- By definition of range, we know that every element in the range of `g ∘ f` is of the form `g (f a)` for some `a ∈ α`.
  have h_range : Set.range (g ∘ f) = g '' Set.range f := by
    grind +splitIndPred;
  simp +decide only [h_range, card_ofFinset];
  refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_image_le ) _;
  exact Finset.card_le_card fun x hx => by aesop;

/-! ## Section 4: Compression Lower Bounds -/

/-
If a type has more than `2^k` elements, no injective encoding into
`k`-bit codes exists. This is the compression impossibility theorem:
you cannot losslessly compress a family of size `> 2^k` into `k` bits.
-/
theorem no_injective_code_of_card_gt
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (hcard : 2^k < Fintype.card α) :
    ¬ ∃ f : α → Fin (2^k), Function.Injective f := by
  exact fun ⟨ f, hf ⟩ => not_le_of_gt hcard ( card_le_of_injective_to_fin f hf )

/-! ## Section 5: Subadditivity Under Products -/

/-
Product encoding: if `α` has at most `2^k` elements and `β` has at most
`2^ℓ` elements, then `α × β` has at most `2^(k + ℓ)` elements.
This is entropy subadditivity: `H(X, Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y)`.
-/
theorem entropyBound_prod_of_entropyBound
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {k ℓ : ℕ}
    (hα : EntropyBound α k) (hβ : EntropyBound β ℓ) :
    EntropyBound (α × β) (k + ℓ) := by
  unfold EntropyBound at *;
  simpa only [ pow_add, Fintype.card_prod ] using Nat.mul_le_mul hα hβ

/-! ## Section 6: Cross-Domain Bridge to Compression-Complexity -/

namespace EntropyComplexityBridge

/-- An invertible compressor with idempotence, length-bounding, and inverse. -/
structure InvertibleCompressor where
  compress : List Bool → List Bool
  decompress : List Bool → List Bool
  hidem : ∀ s, compress (compress s) = compress s
  hlen : ∀ s, (compress s).length ≤ s.length
  hstrict : ∀ s, compress s ≠ s → (compress s).length < s.length
  hinv : ∀ s, decompress (compress s) = s

/-
**Complexity bound implies finite entropy bound (bridge theorem).**

Given an invertible compressor `C` and a finite family of binary strings,
if every element has compressed length ≤ `k`, then the family has at most
`2^(k+1)` elements (since there are `2^(k+1) - 1` binary strings of
length ≤ `k`).

This is the key bridge: algorithmic complexity upper bounds (via compressors)
imply entropy upper bounds (via cardinality control).
-/
theorem complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^(k+1) := by
  -- We know that `compress` is injective and its image is contained in the set of lists of length ≤ k.
  have h_image : Finset.card (Finset.image (fun a => C.compress (embed a)) Finset.univ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
    -- The set of lists of length ≤ k is finite and has cardinality 2^(k+1) - 1.
    have h_card : Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun l => l.length ≤ k) (Finset.biUnion (Finset.range (k + 1)) (fun i => Finset.image (fun l : Fin i → Bool => List.ofFn l) (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin i → Bool)))) ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_filter_le _ _ ) _;
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) _;
      rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun x y hxy => by simpa [ funext_iff ] using hxy ] ; simp +decide [ Nat.geomSum_eq ];
    refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card _ ) h_card;
    simp +decide [ Finset.subset_iff ];
    exact fun a => ⟨ ⟨ _, hbound a, fun i => ( C.compress ( embed a ) |> List.get <| ⟨ i, by linarith [ hbound a, i.2 ] ⟩ ), by simp +decide ⟩, hbound a ⟩;
  rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun a b hab => hembed <| by have := C.hinv ( embed a ) ; have := C.hinv ( embed b ) ; aesop ] at h_image ; exact le_trans h_image ( Nat.sub_le _ _ )

/-- **Finite family complexity certificate.**
If a compressor certifies that every element of a finite type has
compressed representation of length ≤ `k`, this yields an entropy
bound on the type. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_compressor
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    EntropyBound α (k + 1) :=
  complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound C embed hembed hbound

end EntropyComplexityBridge

/-
  # Competitive Exclusion in a Finite Mathematical Ecosystem

  This file develops a small, fully combinatorial model of a finite "mathematical
  ecosystem".  The informal metaphor is that a collection of *theories* compete for
  finitely many *niches*; we keep the mathematics strictly finite and provable and do
  not pursue any informal evolutionary claims.

  ## Objects

  * `T` is a type of *theories* (made `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` where needed).
  * `connections`, `proofDensity`, `axiomCount : T → ℕ` are integer-valued *invariants*
    of a theory.
  * `fitness t = (connections t * proofDensity t) / axiomCount t : ℚ` is a rational
    *fitness score*.  We always work under the hypothesis `0 < axiomCount t`, which keeps
    the denominator nonzero.
  * For an *ecosystem* `E : Finset T`, a *niche assignment* `niche : T → N` (with `N`
    finite) is `AtEquilibrium` on `E` when it is injective on the elements of `E`:
    distinct coexisting theories occupy distinct niches.

  ## Main results

  * `card_le_card_niche` (**packing**): at equilibrium, an ecosystem cannot contain more
    theories than there are niches, `E.card ≤ Fintype.card N`.
  * `competitive_exclusion` (**competitive exclusion**): if there are strictly more
    theories than niches, then two distinct theories must share a niche — a pigeonhole
    statement.
  * `argmax_unique` (**uniqueness of arg-max**): for any function `s : T → α` into a
    linear order, if the values of `s` are pairwise distinct on `E`, then `E` has at most
    one maximizer.  This is stated generically, not tied to `ℚ`.
  * `fitness_max_unique`: the corollary of `argmax_unique` for the `fitness` score.
-/

import Mathlib

namespace CompetitiveExclusion

/-! ## Niche assignments and equilibrium -/

variable {T : Type*} {N : Type*}

/-- A niche assignment `niche : T → N` is **at equilibrium** on an ecosystem `E`
    when it is injective on the elements of `E`: distinct coexisting theories occupy
    distinct niches. -/
def AtEquilibrium (niche : T → N) (E : Finset T) : Prop :=
  Set.InjOn niche (E : Set T)

/-- **Packing theorem.**  At equilibrium, an ecosystem cannot contain more theories
    than there are available niches. -/
theorem card_le_card_niche [Fintype N] {niche : T → N} {E : Finset T}
    (h : AtEquilibrium niche E) : E.card ≤ Fintype.card N := by
  have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (t := (Finset.univ : Finset N)) niche
    (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _) h
  simpa using this

/-- **Competitive exclusion.**  If an ecosystem contains strictly more theories than
    there are niches, then two distinct theories are forced to share a niche. -/
theorem competitive_exclusion [Fintype N] {niche : T → N} {E : Finset T}
    (h : Fintype.card N < E.card) :
    ∃ a ∈ E, ∃ b ∈ E, a ≠ b ∧ niche a = niche b := by
  refine Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to (t := (Finset.univ : Finset N)) ?_
    (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
  simpa using h

/-! ## Uniqueness of the fitness maximizer -/

/-- **Uniqueness of arg-max.**  For a score `s : T → α` into a linearly ordered type,
    if the values of `s` are pairwise distinct on the ecosystem `E`, then any two
    maximizers of `s` on `E` coincide.  Stated generically, not tied to `ℚ`. -/
theorem argmax_unique {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] {s : T → α} {E : Finset T}
    (hinj : Set.InjOn s (E : Set T))
    {x z : T} (hx : x ∈ E) (hz : z ∈ E)
    (hxmax : ∀ y ∈ E, s y ≤ s x) (hzmax : ∀ y ∈ E, s y ≤ s z) :
    z = x :=
  hinj hz hx (le_antisymm (hxmax _ hz) (hzmax _ hx))

/-! ## The fitness score -/

variable (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)

/-- The rational **fitness score** of a theory: the product of its connection count and
    proof density, normalized by its axiom count.  Under `0 < axiomCount t` the
    denominator is nonzero. -/
def fitness (t : T) : ℚ :=
  ((connections t * proofDensity t : ℕ) : ℚ) / (axiomCount t : ℚ)

/-- **Uniqueness of the fitness maximizer.**  If the fitness values are pairwise distinct
    on the ecosystem `E`, then `E` has at most one fitness-maximizing theory. -/
theorem fitness_max_unique {E : Finset T}
    (hinj : Set.InjOn (fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount) (E : Set T))
    {x z : T} (hx : x ∈ E) (hz : z ∈ E)
    (hxmax : ∀ y ∈ E, fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount y
              ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount x)
    (hzmax : ∀ y ∈ E, fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount y
              ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount z) :
    z = x :=
  argmax_unique hinj hx hz hxmax hzmax

end CompetitiveExclusion

* a vertex of odd degree must be the start or the end of the trail;
* there are at most two vertices of odd degree;
* a closed trail (`startVertex = endVertex`) has all even degrees.

The development uses only basic `Finset`/`Fintype` cardinality counting and `Nat` parity.
-/

namespace Eulerian

/-- A finite undirected multigraph with loops: vertices `Fin nV`, edges `Fin nE`, and two
endpoint maps. -/
structure Multigraph (nV nE : ℕ) where
  /-- First endpoint of each edge. -/
  endpt₁ : Fin nE → Fin nV
  /-- Second endpoint of each edge. -/
  endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV

variable {nV nE : ℕ}

/-- The degree of a vertex: the number of endpoint incidences at `v`.  Each edge contributes
once per endpoint slot equal to `v`, so a loop at `v` contributes `2`. -/
def Multigraph.degree (G : Multigraph nV nE) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin nE => G.endpt₁ e = v)).card +
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin nE => G.endpt₂ e = v)).card

/-- An Eulerian trail in `G`: a sequence of `nE + 1` vertices and a permutation of the edges
such that the `i`-th traversed edge `edgePerm i` joins `verts i` to `verts (i+1)` in some
orientation. -/
structure EulerianTrail (G : Multigraph nV nE) where
  /-- The vertices visited, in order. -/
  verts : Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV
  /-- The order in which edges are traversed. -/
  edgePerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin nE)
  /-- The `i`-th traversed edge connects `verts i` and `verts (i+1)`. -/
  connects : ∀ i : Fin nE,
    (G.endpt₁ (edgePerm i) = verts (Fin.castSucc i) ∧ G.endpt₂ (edgePerm i) = verts i.succ) ∨
    (G.endpt₂ (edgePerm i) = verts (Fin.castSucc i) ∧ G.endpt₁ (edgePerm i) = verts i.succ)

variable {G : Multigraph nV nE}

/-- The first vertex of the trail. -/
def EulerianTrail.startVertex (T : EulerianTrail G) : Fin nV := T.verts 0

/-- The last vertex of the trail. -/
def EulerianTrail.endVertex (T : EulerianTrail G) : Fin nV := T.verts (Fin.last nE)

/-- The number of positions at which the trail visits `v`. -/
def EulerianTrail.visitCount (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  Fintype.card {i : Fin (nE + 1) // T.verts i = v}

/-- `1` if the trail starts at `v`, else `0`. -/
def EulerianTrail.startIndicator (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.verts 0 = v then 1 else 0

/-- `1` if the trail ends at `v`, else `0`. -/
def EulerianTrail.endIndicator (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.verts (Fin.last nE) = v then 1 else 0

/-- For a single traversal step `i`, the two endpoint slots of the traversed edge contribute
exactly the same total incidence at `v` as the two consecutive trail vertices. -/
lemma incidence_step (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) (i : Fin nE) :
    (if G.endpt₁ (T.edgePerm i) = v then 1 else 0)
      + (if G.endpt₂ (T.edgePerm i) = v then 1 else 0)
    = (if T.verts (Fin.castSucc i) = v then 1 else 0)
      + (if T.verts i.succ = v then 1 else 0) := by
  cases T.connects i <;> aesop

/-- The degree of `v` equals, summed over traversal steps, the incidence of `v` among the two
consecutive trail vertices at each step. -/
lemma degree_eq_sum (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    G.degree v = ∑ i : Fin nE,
      ((if T.verts (Fin.castSucc i) = v then 1 else 0)
        + (if T.verts i.succ = v then 1 else 0)) := by
  have h_reindex : ∑ i : Fin nE, ((if G.endpt₁ i = v then 1 else 0) + (if G.endpt₂ i = v then 1 else 0)) = ∑ i : Fin nE, ((if T.verts i.castSucc = v then 1 else 0) + (if T.verts i.succ = v then 1 else 0)) := by
    conv_lhs => rw [ ← Equiv.sum_comp T.edgePerm ] ;
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => incidence_step T v i;
  simp_all +decide [ Finset.sum_add_distrib, Multigraph.degree ]

/-- Splitting the visit count of `v` over the trail positions, separating the final position. -/
lemma visitCount_eq_castSucc (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    T.visitCount v
      = (∑ i : Fin nE, if T.verts (Fin.castSucc i) = v then 1 else 0) + T.endIndicator v := by
  unfold EulerianTrail.visitCount EulerianTrail.endIndicator;
  convert Finset.card_filter ( fun i => T.verts i = v ) Finset.univ using 1;
  · rw [ Fintype.subtype_card ];
  · rw [ Fin.sum_univ_castSucc ]

/-- Splitting the visit count of `v` over the trail positions, separating the first position. -/
lemma visitCount_eq_succ (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    T.visitCount v
      = T.startIndicator v + ∑ i : Fin nE, if T.verts i.succ = v then 1 else 0 := by
  convert Fin.sum_univ_succ ( fun x ↦ if T.verts x = v then 1 else 0 ) using 1;
  simp +decide [ EulerianTrail.visitCount, Fintype.card_subtype ]

/-- **Local counting theorem.**  At every vertex, the degree together with the start- and
end-indicators equals twice the number of visits. -/
theorem degree_add_indicators (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    G.degree v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v = 2 * T.visitCount v := by
  have h1 := visitCount_eq_castSucc T v
  have h2 := visitCount_eq_succ T v
  rw [degree_eq_sum T v, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  omega

/-- A vertex of odd degree must be the start or the end of the trail. -/
theorem odd_degree_start_or_end (T : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV)
    (h : Odd (G.degree v)) : v = T.startVertex ∨ v = T.endVertex := by
  simp_all +decide [ EulerianTrail.startVertex, EulerianTrail.endVertex ];
  contrapose! h;
  have := degree_add_indicators T v; simp_all +decide [ Nat.even_iff ] ;
  unfold EulerianTrail.startIndicator EulerianTrail.endIndicator at this; aesop;

/-- There are at most two vertices of odd degree. -/
theorem oddDegree_card_le_two (T : EulerianTrail G) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin nV => Odd (G.degree v))).card ≤ 2 := by
  -- By `odd_degree_start_or_end`, every vertex of odd degree is either `T.startVertex` or `T.endVertex`.
  have h_subset : Finset.filter (fun v => Odd (G.degree v)) Finset.univ ⊆ {T.startVertex, T.endVertex} := by
    grind +suggestions;
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card h_subset ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

/-- A closed trail (start equals end) has all vertices of even degree. -/
theorem closed_trail_even (T : EulerianTrail G) (h : T.startVertex = T.endVertex)
    (v : Fin nV) : Even (G.degree v) := by
  by_contra h_odd;
  -- By `odd_degree_start_or_end T v`, `v = T.startVertex ∨ v = T.endVertex`.
  have h_start_or_end : v = T.startVertex ∨ v = T.endVertex := by
    exact odd_degree_start_or_end T v <| by simpa using h_odd;
  -- Using `startVertex = verts 0`, `endVertex = verts last`, and `Eq.symm`, in both cases `v = T.startVertex = T.endVertex`.
  have h_eq : T.startIndicator v = 1 ∧ T.endIndicator v = 1 := by
    cases h_start_or_end <;> simp_all +decide [ EulerianTrail.startIndicator, EulerianTrail.endIndicator ]; all_goals exact ⟨ h, rfl ⟩;
  exact h_odd ( by rw [ Nat.even_iff ] ; have := degree_add_indicators T v; omega )

end Eulerian

import Mathlib

/-!
# Entropy-Complexity Bridge: From Compression to Information Bounds

This file establishes formal bridges between algorithmic compression/complexity
and entropy-like information bounds on finite types. The central theme is:

> **Compression controls entropy-like support complexity.**
> If a finite family of objects can be injectively encoded into a bounded
> code space, then the family's cardinality (and hence its log-cardinality,
> a uniform entropy surrogate) is bounded by the code space size.

## Main Results

### Finite cardinality bounds from injective encodings
- `card_le_of_injective_to_fin`: Injective map to `Fin N` bounds cardinality by `N`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code`: Injective map to `Fin (2^k)` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode`: Injective map to `Fin k → Bool` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound`: Range of a map to `Fin (2^k)` has size ≤ `2^k`.

### Entropy bounds
- `EntropyBound`: Predicate `Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k`, the finite uniform entropy inequality.
- `entropyBound_of_injective_code`: Injective code implies entropy bound.
- `uniform_entropy_le_code_length`: Log-cardinality bounded by code length.

### Support monotonicity (data processing)
- `support_entropy_monotone_under_map`: `|range f| ≤ |α|`.
- `card_range_le_card_codomain`: `|range f| ≤ |β|`.
- `support_entropy_comp_monotone`: `|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|` — deterministic data processing.

### Cross-domain bridge
- `complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound`: Connects compressor bounds
  to finite cardinality control.

## Mathematical Significance

These theorems form the combinatorial skeleton of the source coding principle
and create a formal route from Kolmogorov-style complexity bounds to
entropy/information inequalities. The composition monotonicity theorem
`support_entropy_comp_monotone` is a combinatorial shadow of the
**data processing inequality**: deterministic post-processing cannot
increase the number of distinguishable outputs.
-/

open Set Function Finset Fintype

/-! ## Section 1: Core Finite Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- An injective map from a finite type to `Fin N` implies the source has
at most `N` elements. This is the fundamental counting principle underlying
all compression-to-entropy arguments. -/
theorem card_le_of_injective_to_fin
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {N : ℕ}
    (f : α → Fin N) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ N := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin N) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = N := Fintype.card_fin N

/-- An injective encoding into `Fin (2^k)` bounds source cardinality by `2^k`.
This is the exponential form of the entropy bound: if objects can be
described by `k`-bit codes, there are at most `2^k` of them. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k :=
  card_le_of_injective_to_fin enc henc

/-- The cardinality of the function space `Fin k → Bool` is exactly `2^k`.
This witnesses bitstrings of length `k` as a code space of size `2^k`. -/
theorem fintype_card_fun_bool (k : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) = 2^k := by
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]

/-- An injective encoding into explicit bitstrings `Fin k → Bool` bounds
cardinality by `2^k`. This is the most concrete form: each element gets
a unique `k`-bit string, so there can be at most `2^k` elements. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (f : α → (Fin k → Bool)) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = 2^k := fintype_card_fun_bool k

/-- The range of any map into `Fin (2^k)` has at most `2^k` elements.
This does not require injectivity — it bounds the number of distinguishable
outputs of any encoding scheme. -/
theorem card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound
    {n k : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin (2^k)) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^k)) := Fintype.card_subtype_le _
    _ = 2^k := Fintype.card_fin _

/-! ## Section 2: Entropy Bound Predicate and Logarithmic Form -/

/-- `EntropyBound α k` asserts that the uniform entropy of the finite type `α`
is at most `k` bits: equivalently, `|α| ≤ 2^k`. This is the finite
combinatorial skeleton of the source coding bound `H(X) ≤ k` for a
uniform source over `α` encoded with `k`-bit codewords. -/
def EntropyBound (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k

/-- An injective encoding into `k`-bit codes implies the entropy bound.
This is the formal finite-uniform entropy inequality: if every element
of `α` receives a unique `k`-bit code, then `H(α) ≤ k`. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    EntropyBound α k :=
  card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc

/-
Logarithmic form of the entropy bound: if `α` injects into `Fin (2^k)`,
then `log₂ |α| ≤ k`. Uses `Nat.log` which is the floor of the logarithm.
-/
theorem uniform_entropy_le_code_length
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k := by
  -- We have card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code which gives Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k.
  -- Taking the base-2 logarithm is monotonic, so log₂ |α| ≤ log₂ 2^k = k.
  have hcard : Fintype.card α ≤ 2 ^ k := by
    apply card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc
  exact (Nat.log_mono_right hcard).trans (Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2) k).le

/-- For any injective encoding `α → Fin (2^k)`, the
log-cardinality of `α` is bounded by `k`. -/
theorem log_card_range_le_of_embedding_into_bitstrings
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k :=
  uniform_entropy_le_code_length enc henc

/-! ## Section 3: Support Monotonicity — Data Processing -/

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as its domain.
This is a combinatorial form of the principle that deterministic
processing cannot create new distinguishable outputs. -/
theorem support_entropy_monotone_under_map
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card α :=
  Fintype.card_range_le f

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as the codomain.
This is the trivial but useful fact that range ⊆ codomain implies
the cardinality inequality. -/
theorem card_range_le_card_codomain
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card β :=
  Fintype.card_subtype_le _

/-
**Combinatorial Data Processing Inequality.**
Composition cannot increase the number of distinguishable outputs:
`|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|`. This is the finite combinatorial
shadow of the data processing inequality `H(g(X)) ≤ H(X)` for
deterministic channels.
-/
theorem support_entropy_comp_monotone
    {α β γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range (g ∘ f)) ≤ Fintype.card (Set.range f) := by
  -- By definition of range, we know that every element in the range of `g ∘ f` is of the form `g (f a)` for some `a ∈ α`.
  have h_range : Set.range (g ∘ f) = g '' Set.range f := by
    grind +splitIndPred;
  simp +decide only [h_range, card_ofFinset];
  refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_image_le ) _;
  exact Finset.card_le_card fun x hx => by aesop;

/-! ## Section 4: Compression Lower Bounds -/

/-
If a type has more than `2^k` elements, no injective encoding into
`k`-bit codes exists. This is the compression impossibility theorem:
you cannot losslessly compress a family of size `> 2^k` into `k` bits.
-/
theorem no_injective_code_of_card_gt
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (hcard : 2^k < Fintype.card α) :
    ¬ ∃ f : α → Fin (2^k), Function.Injective f := by
  exact fun ⟨ f, hf ⟩ => not_le_of_gt hcard ( card_le_of_injective_to_fin f hf )

/-! ## Section 5: Subadditivity Under Products -/

/-
Product encoding: if `α` has at most `2^k` elements and `β` has at most
`2^ℓ` elements, then `α × β` has at most `2^(k + ℓ)` elements.
This is entropy subadditivity: `H(X, Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y)`.
-/
theorem entropyBound_prod_of_entropyBound
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {k ℓ : ℕ}
    (hα : EntropyBound α k) (hβ : EntropyBound β ℓ) :
    EntropyBound (α × β) (k + ℓ) := by
  unfold EntropyBound at *;
  simpa only [ pow_add, Fintype.card_prod ] using Nat.mul_le_mul hα hβ

/-! ## Section 6: Cross-Domain Bridge to Compression-Complexity -/

namespace EntropyComplexityBridge

/-- An invertible compressor with idempotence, length-bounding, and inverse. -/
structure InvertibleCompressor where
  compress : List Bool → List Bool
  decompress : List Bool → List Bool
  hidem : ∀ s, compress (compress s) = compress s
  hlen : ∀ s, (compress s).length ≤ s.length
  hstrict : ∀ s, compress s ≠ s → (compress s).length < s.length
  hinv : ∀ s, decompress (compress s) = s

/-
**Complexity bound implies finite entropy bound (bridge theorem).**

Given an invertible compressor `C` and a finite family of binary strings,
if every element has compressed length ≤ `k`, then the family has at most
`2^(k+1)` elements (since there are `2^(k+1) - 1` binary strings of
length ≤ `k`).

This is the key bridge: algorithmic complexity upper bounds (via compressors)
imply entropy upper bounds (via cardinality control).
-/
theorem complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^(k+1) := by
  -- We know that `compress` is injective and its image is contained in the set of lists of length ≤ k.
  have h_image : Finset.card (Finset.image (fun a => C.compress (embed a)) Finset.univ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
    -- The set of lists of length ≤ k is finite and has cardinality 2^(k+1) - 1.
    have h_card : Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun l => l.length ≤ k) (Finset.biUnion (Finset.range (k + 1)) (fun i => Finset.image (fun l : Fin i → Bool => List.ofFn l) (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin i → Bool)))) ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_filter_le _ _ ) _;
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) _;
      rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun x y hxy => by simpa [ funext_iff ] using hxy ] ; simp +decide [ Nat.geomSum_eq ];
    refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card _ ) h_card;
    simp +decide [ Finset.subset_iff ];
    exact fun a => ⟨ ⟨ _, hbound a, fun i => ( C.compress ( embed a ) |> List.get <| ⟨ i, by linarith [ hbound a, i.2 ] ⟩ ), by simp +decide ⟩, hbound a ⟩;
  rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun a b hab => hembed <| by have := C.hinv ( embed a ) ; have := C.hinv ( embed b ) ; aesop ] at h_image ; exact le_trans h_image ( Nat.sub_le _ _ )

/-- **Finite family complexity certificate.**
If a compressor certifies that every element of a finite type has
compressed representation of length ≤ `k`, this yields an entropy
bound on the type. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_compressor
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    EntropyBound α (k + 1) :=
  complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound C embed hembed hbound

end EntropyComplexityBridge

/-!
# Entropy-Complexity Bridge: From Compression to Information Bounds

This file establishes formal bridges between algorithmic compression/complexity
and entropy-like information bounds on finite types. The central theme is:

> **Compression controls entropy-like support complexity.**
> If a finite family of objects can be injectively encoded into a bounded
> code space, then the family's cardinality (and hence its log-cardinality,
> a uniform entropy surrogate) is bounded by the code space size.

### Finite cardinality bounds from injective encodings
- `card_le_of_injective_to_fin`: Injective map to `Fin N` bounds cardinality by `N`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code`: Injective map to `Fin (2^k)` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode`: Injective map to `Fin k → Bool` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound`: Range of a map to `Fin (2^k)` has size ≤ `2^k`.

- `EntropyBound`: Predicate `Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k`, the finite uniform entropy inequality.
- `entropyBound_of_injective_code`: Injective code implies entropy bound.
- `uniform_entropy_le_code_length`: Log-cardinality bounded by code length.

- `card_range_le_card_codomain`: `|range f| ≤ |β|`.

- `complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound`: Connects compressor bounds
  to finite cardinality control.

## Mathematical Significance

These theorems form the combinatorial skeleton of the source coding principle
and create a formal route from Kolmogorov-style complexity bounds to
entropy/information inequalities. The composition monotonicity theorem
`support_entropy_comp_monotone` is a combinatorial shadow of the
**data processing inequality**: deterministic post-processing cannot
increase the number of distinguishable outputs.

open Set Function Finset Fintype

/-! ## Section 1: Core Finite Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- An injective map from a finite type to `Fin N` implies the source has
at most `N` elements. This is the fundamental counting principle underlying
all compression-to-entropy arguments. -/
theorem card_le_of_injective_to_fin
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {N : ℕ}
    (f : α → Fin N) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ N := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin N) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = N := Fintype.card_fin N

/-- An injective encoding into `Fin (2^k)` bounds source cardinality by `2^k`.
This is the exponential form of the entropy bound: if objects can be
described by `k`-bit codes, there are at most `2^k` of them. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k :=
  card_le_of_injective_to_fin enc henc

/-- The cardinality of the function space `Fin k → Bool` is exactly `2^k`.

theorem fintype_card_fun_bool (k : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) = 2^k := by
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]

cardinality by `2^k`. This is the most concrete form: each element gets
a unique `k`-bit string, so there can be at most `2^k` elements. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (f : α → (Fin k → Bool)) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = 2^k := fintype_card_fun_bool k

outputs of any encoding scheme. -/

    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^k)) := Fintype.card_subtype_le _

/-- `EntropyBound α k` asserts that the uniform entropy of the finite type `α`

combinatorial skeleton of the source coding bound `H(X) ≤ k` for a
uniform source over `α` encoded with `k`-bit codewords. -/

of `α` receives a unique `k`-bit code, then `H(α) ≤ k`. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_injective_code

then `log₂ |α| ≤ k`. Uses `Nat.log` which is the floor of the logarithm.
-/
theorem uniform_entropy_le_code_length

    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k := by
  -- We have card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code which gives Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k.
  -- Taking the base-2 logarithm is monotonic, so log₂ |α| ≤ log₂ 2^k = k.
  have hcard : Fintype.card α ≤ 2 ^ k := by

theorem support_entropy_monotone_under_map
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]

shadow of the data processing inequality `H(g(X)) ≤ H(X)` for

  exact Finset.card_le_card fun x hx => by aesop;

/-
If a type has more than `2^k` elements, no injective encoding into
`k`-bit codes exists. This is the compression impossibility theorem:
you cannot losslessly compress a family of size `> 2^k` into `k` bits.
-/
theorem no_injective_code_of_card_gt
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (hcard : 2^k < Fintype.card α) :

  exact fun ⟨ f, hf ⟩ => not_le_of_gt hcard ( card_le_of_injective_to_fin f hf )

/-
Product encoding: if `α` has at most `2^k` elements and `β` has at most
`2^ℓ` elements, then `α × β` has at most `2^(k + ℓ)` elements.
This is entropy subadditivity: `H(X, Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y)`.
-/
theorem entropyBound_prod_of_entropyBound
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {k ℓ : ℕ}
    (hα : EntropyBound α k) (hβ : EntropyBound β ℓ) :
    EntropyBound (α × β) (k + ℓ) := by
  unfold EntropyBound at *;
  simpa only [ pow_add, Fintype.card_prod ] using Nat.mul_le_mul hα hβ

/-! ## Section 6: Cross-Domain Bridge to Compression-Complexity -/

namespace EntropyComplexityBridge

/-- An invertible compressor with idempotence, length-bounding, and inverse. -/
structure InvertibleCompressor where
  compress : List Bool → List Bool
  decompress : List Bool → List Bool
  hidem : ∀ s, compress (compress s) = compress s
  hlen : ∀ s, (compress s).length ≤ s.length
  hstrict : ∀ s, compress s ≠ s → (compress s).length < s.length
  hinv : ∀ s, decompress (compress s) = s

/-
**Complexity bound implies finite entropy bound (bridge theorem).**

Given an invertible compressor `C` and a finite family of binary strings,
if every element has compressed length ≤ `k`, then the family has at most

length ≤ `k`).

This is the key bridge: algorithmic complexity upper bounds (via compressors)
imply entropy upper bounds (via cardinality control).
-/
theorem complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :

compressed representation of length ≤ `k`, this yields an entropy
bound on the type. -/

  # Eulerian Trails in Finite Undirected Multigraphs

  A self-contained development of Eulerian trails in finite undirected
  multigraphs, with no category-theoretic content.

  ## Representation

  A multigraph is given by a vertex type `V`, an edge type `E`, and two
  endpoint maps `fst, snd : E → V`.  The graph is *undirected*: the orientation
  of an edge is irrelevant and is only used to talk about traversals.  Loops
  (edges with `fst e = snd e`) are allowed and contribute `2` to a vertex
  degree, and parallel edges are allowed since `E` is an arbitrary type.

  A *walk* is a starting vertex together with a list of steps `(e, v)`, each
  meaning "traverse edge `e`, arriving at `v`".  A walk is *valid* if every
  edge actually connects its two consecutive vertices (in either orientation).
  A *trail* additionally uses no edge twice, and an *Eulerian trail* uses every
  edge exactly once.

  ## Main results

  * `Multigraph.incidence_count_identity` — the core incidence identity:
    for any valid walk, the total endpoint-incidence at a vertex `w` plus the
    start/end correction terms equals twice the number of times `w` is visited.
  * `Multigraph.degree_add_endpoints` — the specialization to Eulerian trails:
    `degree w + [s = w] + [t = w] = 2 * (visits of w)`.
  * `Multigraph.even_degree_of_ne_endpoints` — every non-endpoint vertex has
    even degree.
  * `Multigraph.odd_degree_card_le_two` — a multigraph with an Eulerian trail
    has at most two odd-degree vertices.
  * `Multigraph.all_even_of_closed` — for a closed Eulerian trail (`s = t`),
    every vertex has even degree.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace EulerianMultigraph

open Finset

/-- A finite undirected multigraph: a vertex type, an edge type, and two
endpoint maps.  Orientation is irrelevant for the undirected structure; it is
only used to describe traversals. -/
structure Multigraph (V : Type*) (E : Type*) where
  /-- One endpoint of each edge. -/
  fst : E → V
  /-- The other endpoint of each edge. -/
  snd : E → V

variable {V : Type*} {E : Type*}

/-- The list of edges used by a sequence of steps. -/
def usedEdges (steps : List (E × V)) : List E := steps.map Prod.fst

namespace Multigraph

/-- Edge `e` connects vertices `a` and `b` (in either orientation). -/
def Connects (G : Multigraph V E) (e : E) (a b : V) : Prop :=
  (G.fst e = a ∧ G.snd e = b) ∨ (G.fst e = b ∧ G.snd e = a)

/-- A walk starting at `a` and following the given steps is *valid* if every
edge connects its two consecutive vertices. -/
def IsValidWalk (G : Multigraph V E) : V → List (E × V) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | a, (e, b) :: rest => G.Connects e a b ∧ G.IsValidWalk b rest

/-- The list of vertices visited by a walk starting at `a`. -/
def visited (G : Multigraph V E) : V → List (E × V) → List V
  | a, [] => [a]
  | a, (_, b) :: rest => a :: G.visited b rest

/-- The final vertex of a walk starting at `a`. -/
def endVertex (G : Multigraph V E) : V → List (E × V) → V
  | a, [] => a
  | _, (_, b) :: rest => G.endVertex b rest

variable (G : Multigraph V E)

/-- The total endpoint-incidence of the edges used by a walk at the vertex `w`:
each used edge contributes `1` for each of its endpoints equal to `w` (so a loop
at `w` contributes `2`). -/
def edgeIncidenceSum [DecidableEq V] (w : V) (steps : List (E × V)) : ℕ :=
  ((usedEdges steps).map
    (fun e => (if G.fst e = w then 1 else 0) + (if G.snd e = w then 1 else 0))).sum

/-- The degree of a vertex `w`: the number of edge-endpoints equal to `w`,
counting loops twice. -/
def degree [DecidableEq V] [Fintype E] (w : V) : ℕ :=
  ∑ e : E, ((if G.fst e = w then 1 else 0) + (if G.snd e = w then 1 else 0))

/-- An Eulerian trail from `s` to `t`: a valid walk ending at `t` that uses
every edge exactly once. -/
def IsEulerianTrail [DecidableEq E] (s t : V) (steps : List (E × V)) : Prop :=
  G.IsValidWalk s steps ∧ G.endVertex s steps = t ∧
    ∀ e : E, (usedEdges steps).count e = 1

/-- A multigraph *has* an Eulerian trail from `s` to `t`. -/
def HasEulerianTrail [DecidableEq E] (s t : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ steps, G.IsEulerianTrail s t steps

/-! ### The core incidence identity -/

/-- **Core incidence identity.**  For any valid walk starting at `a`, the total
endpoint-incidence at a vertex `w` over the used edges, plus a `1` for each of
the start vertex `a` and the end vertex equal to `w`, equals twice the number of
times `w` is visited.  Intuitively, each visit to `w` consumes two incidences
(one to enter, one to leave) except that the start and end vertices have one
unmatched incidence each. -/
theorem incidence_count_identity [DecidableEq V] (w : V) :
    ∀ (a : V) (steps : List (E × V)), G.IsValidWalk a steps →
      G.edgeIncidenceSum w steps + (if a = w then 1 else 0)
          + (if G.endVertex a steps = w then 1 else 0)
        = 2 * (G.visited a steps).count w := by
  intro a steps h;
  induction' steps with e steps ih generalizing a; all_goals grind +locals

/-! ### From the incidence identity to degrees -/

/-- For a walk that uses every edge exactly once, the endpoint-incidence sum at
`w` equals the degree of `w`. -/
theorem edgeIncidenceSum_eq_degree [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] (w : V)
    (steps : List (E × V)) (h : ∀ e : E, (usedEdges steps).count e = 1) :
    G.edgeIncidenceSum w steps = G.degree w := by
  have h_finset : (usedEdges steps).toFinset = Finset.univ := by
    exact Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun e => List.mem_toFinset.mpr ( List.count_pos_iff.mp ( by linarith [ h e ] ) );
  convert Finset.sum_list_map_count ( usedEdges steps ) ( fun e => ( if G.fst e = w then 1 else 0 ) + ( if G.snd e = w then 1 else 0 ) ) using 1;
  aesop

/-- **Degree identity for Eulerian trails.**  If `steps` is an Eulerian trail
from `s` to `t`, then for every vertex `w`,
`degree w + [s = w] + [t = w] = 2 * (number of visits of w)`. -/
theorem degree_add_endpoints [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s t w : V}
    {steps : List (E × V)} (h : G.IsEulerianTrail s t steps) :
    G.degree w + (if s = w then 1 else 0) + (if t = w then 1 else 0)
      = 2 * (G.visited s steps).count w := by
  convert incidence_count_identity G w s steps h.1 using 1;
  rw [ edgeIncidenceSum_eq_degree G w steps h.2.2, h.2.1 ]

/-! ### Parity consequences -/

/-- Every vertex other than the two endpoints of an Eulerian trail has even
degree. -/
theorem even_degree_of_ne_endpoints [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s t w : V}
    (h : G.HasEulerianTrail s t) (hs : w ≠ s) (ht : w ≠ t) :
    Even (G.degree w) := by
  -- Apply the degreeAddEndpoints theorem to the Eulerian trail.
  obtain ⟨steps, hsteps⟩ := h
  have h_deg : G.degree w + (if s = w then 1 else 0) + (if t = w then 1 else 0) = 2 * (G.visited s steps).count w := by
    grind +suggestions;
  grind

/-- An odd-degree vertex must be one of the two endpoints of an Eulerian trail. -/
theorem eq_endpoint_of_odd_degree [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s t w : V}
    (h : G.HasEulerianTrail s t) (hw : Odd (G.degree w)) :
    w = s ∨ w = t := by
  exact Classical.not_not.1 fun away => absurd ( even_degree_of_ne_endpoints G h ( by tauto ) ( by tauto ) ) ( by simpa using hw )

/-- **Main theorem.**  A finite multigraph admitting an Eulerian trail has at
most two odd-degree vertices. -/
theorem odd_degree_card_le_two [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s t : V}
    (h : G.HasEulerianTrail s t) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun w => Odd (G.degree w))).card ≤ 2 := by
  have h_subset : Finset.filter (fun w => Odd (G.degree w)) Finset.univ ⊆ {s, t} := by
    grind +suggestions;
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card h_subset ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

/-- **Closed-trail corollary.**  If a multigraph admits a closed Eulerian trail
(`s = t`), then every vertex has even degree. -/
theorem all_even_of_closed [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s : V}
    (h : G.HasEulerianTrail s s) (w : V) :
    Even (G.degree w) := by
  -- Apply the degree_add_endpoints theorem to conclude that G.degree w is even.
  have h_even : ∀ w, G.degree w + (if s = w then 1 else 0) + (if s = w then 1 else 0) = 2 * (G.visited s h.choose).count w := by
    exact fun w => by simpa using degree_add_endpoints G ( h.choose_spec ) ;
  grind +splitImp

import Mathlib

/-!
# Eulerian trails imply at most two odd-degree vertices

This file is a minimal, self-contained formalization of the classical parity
theorem for Eulerian trails on finite multigraphs.

A finite multigraph is encoded by an endpoint map `ends : Fin nE → Fin nV × Fin nV`,
sending each edge index to an *ordered* pair of vertices.  The `degree` of a vertex
is the number of edge endpoints incident to it: each edge contributes `1` for each
of its two endpoints equal to `v`, so a loop at `v` contributes `2`.

An `EulerianTrail` is a walk that uses every edge exactly once: a vertex sequence
`walk : Fin (nE+1) → Fin nV` together with a permutation `edgeAt` of the edges such
that the `i`-th step of the walk traverses edge `edgeAt i` (in either orientation).

The main results are:

* `degree_eq_walk_sum` — the degree of `v` is the sum over walk steps of the number
  of the two consecutive walk positions equal to `v`;
* `degree_add_endpoints` — a telescoping/endpoint-correction identity:
  `degree v + (start-indicator + end-indicator) = 2 * (number of walk positions = v)`;
* `even_degree_of_internal` — a vertex that is neither the start nor the end of the
  trail has even degree;
* `odd_degree_mem_endpoints` — an odd-degree vertex must be the start or the end;
* `odd_degree_vertices_le_two` — there are at most two odd-degree vertices.
-/

namespace EulerianTrailParity

open Finset

/-- A finite multigraph on `nV` vertices and `nE` edges, encoded by an endpoint map
sending each edge to an ordered pair of vertices. -/
structure Multigraph (nV nE : ℕ) where
  /-- The ordered pair of endpoints of each edge. -/
  ends : Fin nE → Fin nV × Fin nV

variable {nV nE : ℕ}

/-- The degree of a vertex `v`: the number of edge endpoints equal to `v`.
Each edge contributes the sum of two indicators (one per endpoint), so a loop at `v`
contributes `2`. -/
def degree (G : Multigraph nV nE) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ e : Fin nE,
    ((if (G.ends e).1 = v then 1 else 0) + (if (G.ends e).2 = v then 1 else 0))

/-- An Eulerian trail of `G`: a vertex sequence `walk` together with a permutation
`edgeAt` of the edges, such that the `i`-th step traverses edge `edgeAt i` between the
consecutive walk vertices (in either orientation). -/
structure EulerianTrail (G : Multigraph nV nE) where
  /-- The sequence of `nE + 1` vertices visited by the trail. -/
  walk : Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV
  /-- The order in which the edges are traversed. -/
  edgeAt : Equiv.Perm (Fin nE)
  /-- The `i`-th step traverses edge `edgeAt i` between `walk i` and `walk (i+1)`. -/
  compat : ∀ i : Fin nE,
    G.ends (edgeAt i) = (walk i.castSucc, walk i.succ) ∨
    G.ends (edgeAt i) = (walk i.succ, walk i.castSucc)

/-
**Degree/incidence identity (A).** The degree of `v` equals the sum, over walk
steps, of the number of the two consecutive walk positions equal to `v`.
-/
theorem degree_eq_walk_sum (G : Multigraph nV nE) (et : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    degree G v =
      ∑ i : Fin nE,
        ((if et.walk i.castSucc = v then 1 else 0) +
         (if et.walk i.succ = v then 1 else 0)) := by
  unfold degree;
  rw [ ← Equiv.sum_comp et.edgeAt ];
  grind +suggestions

/-
**Endpoint-correction identity.** Adding the start and end indicators to the degree
yields twice the number of walk positions equal to `v`.
-/
theorem degree_add_endpoints (G : Multigraph nV nE) (et : EulerianTrail G) (v : Fin nV) :
    degree G v +
        ((if et.walk 0 = v then 1 else 0) +
         (if et.walk (Fin.last nE) = v then 1 else 0))
